analysis.title: Global Weekly Kickstart: Quality Regains Ground, Momentum Faces Headwinds
key_insights: Global equities face a higher cost of capital. Credit and sovereign spreads are widening, cyclical exposure is being cut, and weaker balance sheets are under pressure.
The Quality long-short pair has risen 12% in the US and 5% in Europe since its September low. GS expects the rotation could continue.
US earnings growth is expected to slow from 30% in 2026 to c.15% in 2027, and European earnings growth from 20% to below 10%, while higher energy costs pressure margins.

Narrow market breadth adds risk. The gap between headline indices and the median stock can close through a catch-up by laggards or a catch-down by recent winners. Both outcomes imply a Momentum reversal.
Quality looks attractive in a catch-down scenario because positioning remains light and valuations are less demanding.
GS favours selective Quality exposure rather than a broad defensive shift, because lower inflation, energy prices and interest rates remain the economists' base case.

Global equities fell 1.6% last week as risk appetite deteriorated and Momentum reversed. Technology led the correction at -7%, EM and Asia fell around 5%, and Europe outperformed on lower AI exposure and its Value characteristics.
US 10y yields fell by 17bp last week.
Semiconductors & Equipment fell 9.7% in the US and 17.1% in Japan on the week. Korea's market fell 15.8% and Taiwan's 6.5% in USD terms. Korea's IT sector fell 19.4%.
Consensus EPS growth for the S&P 500 is 31.9% in 2026E and 15.4% in 2027E. IT is expected to grow EPS 88.0% in 2026E and 42.3% in 2027E, while Energy EPS is expected to fall 10.8% in 2027E.
GS 12-month targets: S&P 500 8700 (+13.6%), STOXX 600 695, MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan 1120 (+34.7%), Topix 4600. GS forecasts the US 10Y yield falling to 4.4% and Brent to $75 over 12 months.
GS Bull/Bear Market Indicator stands at 66%, with the Shiller PE at 40.2 (97th percentile) and unemployment at 4.2%.

The week ahead has no Fed speakers because of the blackout period before the FOMC. Data includes the US S&P PMI, UK labour and inflation data, flash October PMIs in Europe, Japan core CPI, and China Q3 GDP.
Central bank meetings are due this week in Korea, Indonesia and the Philippines.

earnings_insights: GS top-down 2026 EPS growth estimates (exhibit 7) are 36% for the S&P 500 and 15% for STOXX 600, versus bottom-up consensus of 32% and 21%. These are estimates, not reported figures.
Consensus net margins (estimates): S&P 500 16.2% in 2026E and 17.0% in 2027E. IT 29.1% and 31.2%.
Consensus sales growth (estimates): S&P 500 12.0% 2026E and 8.7% 2027E. IT 40.8% and 30.7%. Energy sales are expected at +22.7% in 2026E and -6.8% in 2027E.

trade_ideas.description: Selective Quality exposure, via the Quality long-short pair, rather than a broad defensive shift
trade_ideas.rationale: Quality benefits if narrow breadth resolves through a catch-down, with light positioning and less demanding valuations.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower inflation, energy prices and interest rates remain the base case, which argues against a broad defensive rotation.

risk_factors: Narrow market breadth, with either a catch-up or catch-down implying a Momentum reversal.
Higher cost of capital, with credit and sovereign spreads widening.
Slowing earnings growth in 2027 in the US and Europe.
Concentration in AI and technology, which led last week's correction.

tension_points.bull_case: Laggards catch up with headline indices, broadening the market.
tension_points.bear_case: Recent winners catch down to the median stock. Either path implies a Momentum reversal, and Quality looks attractive in a catch-down because positioning is light and valuations less demanding.
